newsitem.title: USA: Latin debts pull back with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Latin debts pull back with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: The pause in U.S. Treasuries rally cooled the fever in Latin Bradies, while other emerging market debts caught up belatedly, traders and analysts said.

Brazil eked out small gains on the day as its Senate economic affairs committee passed a bill to allow the swap and buyback of sovereign debts. The vote has been widely expected and discounted in the market, traders said.
There was some profit-taking on the news, they noted.
"The approval means that government now can legally retire the debt," said Ingrid Iverson, Brady strategist at UBS Securities. "It is positive in the sense that it reduces the supply."

With no cap attached to the buyback authorization, Brazil could theoretically purchase all its Bradies, although the government is unlikely to come up with the fiscal resources to do so, she said. Brazil's outstanding Bradies have a face amount of $49.6 billion and estimated market value of $36.7 billion.

The Brazilian government is known to have bought back some of its debts on the market and it may continue to do so. Or it could issue new uncollateralized bonds to exchange the Bradies like Mexico and the Philippines, she added.

Argentina was heading to calmer waters as the International Monetary Fund is backing the fiscal plan of the economy minister Roque Fernandez. A letter of intent outlining revised IMF targets is to be released later.
But with Argentina FRBs penetrating 80, some retracement was to be expected, traders said. It was unchanged at 80-1/2.
Mexico Pars and Discount were underpinned by rising oil prices, which could trigger warrant payments on December 31.
The biggest gainers on the day are Nigeria, Bulgaria and Russia, which tend to march to their own drummers different from U.S. Treasuries.
Nigeria Pars, another beneficiary of higher oil prices, rose 1-1/8 to 56.00
Bulgaria clawed back from the drastic selloff last week when IMF delayed disbursement of loans. Bulgaria FLRB rose one to 29-1/4.

Russia Vnesh loans and MinFin bonds all made new gains. President Boris Yeltsin's transferring key authorities to the market-friendly prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was seen as reassuring to investors.
